text: Hold a plastic bag over a fire, let go, and it flies! Congratulations, you've built a hot-air balloon!
Whoa!
Hot air spreads out, so a box of it weighs less than a box of cold air.
But once it cools down, it sinks right back... and lands on Ben.
That bag lifts a cookie. But not Ben.
Come on!
One cubic metre of hot air lifts about a sandwich. Ben needs six hundred of them.
So you sew up a bag the size of a house.
Are those my bedsheets?
Blow cold air in with a fan to open it up,
then fire the burner. The hot air stands it up!
Ben climbs in with a sandwich,
you untie the rope, and up, up, up he goes!
The hotter the air inside, the harder it lifts.
Lunch time!
So he turns the burner off.
But the air inside cools down, and below sixty-seven degrees it can't hold him up,
so it sinks, right towards the neighbour.
My sandwich!
Right on target.
Ben fires the burner, but the air takes a few seconds to heat up, so it keeps on sinking.
Hey! My roof!
And balloons don't come with a steering wheel, Ben.
But the wind blows different ways at different heights,
so you climb into the wind that goes your way.
Next stop: grandma's garden, round the corner.
To come down, pull the vent. Hot air rushes out of the top,
and down, down, down you go.
Too much! Too much!
The basket hits the lawn, and the wind drags it along,
until the whole thing flops over the washing line.
Congratulations, you've built a hot-air balloon!
You could have taken the bus, dear.
I know.
